title: How to Block Spam Calls and Texts on Android (India)
html:
On Android, start in the Phone app: make sure caller ID and spam protection is on, then block and report every spam number you get. For fraud calls and messages in India, also report them on Sanchar Saathi's Chakshu. DND registration with TRAI covers promotional calls, but it will not stop scammers, so do not rely on it alone.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Menu names vary by brand; the steps below are for the Google Phone and Messages apps. Samsung and other brands have their own dialer with similar options.

I checked the Google Phone app's Caller ID and spam settings on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 on 10 Oct 2026. The Google Messages steps come from Google's help page and I did not test them on this phone.

1. Turn on spam filtering in the Phone app

In the Google Phone app, tap More, then Settings, then Caller ID and spam. Google says caller ID and spam protection is on by default. Turn on "Filter spam calls" and spam calls will no longer give you missed-call notifications, though you can still find them in your call history and voicemail. When a call looks like spam, the screen shows "Suspected spam caller" or "Spam", and you can answer, block or report it.

2. Block and report a number

Open the Phone app, tap More, then Call history, pick a call from the number, and tap Block / report spam. To block calls from private or unknown numbers, go to More, then Settings, then Blocked numbers, and turn on "Unknown". To undo a block, go to Blocked numbers, tap the clear icon next to the number, and choose Unblock. Blocked calls will not appear in your call history.

3. Texts: block and report in Messages

In Google Messages, touch and hold the conversation, tap Block, then Report spam, then OK. From inside a conversation you can use More options, then Details, then Block and report spam. Reporting also blocks the sender and moves the message to the "Spam and blocked" folder. Google says the spammer cannot see your report, and your name and number are not linked to their messages.

Do not tap links in a text you did not expect, and do not call back a number it tells you to call. See how to spot a phishing message.

4. In India: report fraud calls and messages on Chakshu

Sanchar Saathi, the Department of Telecommunications portal, has a service called Chakshu for reporting suspected fraud communication. You can report calls, SMS or WhatsApp messages that try to defraud telecom users, such as KYC update, bank account, SIM, gas or electricity bill messages, impersonation of a government official, or sextortion. The portal says to report within 30 days. It also has a link for spam (unsolicited commercial communication).

The portal also says: if you have already lost money, report it on the cybercrime helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in. Do that first, and quickly. Our guide on reporting online fraud in India has the steps.

5. DND (Do Not Disturb)

TRAI's Preference Registration page says you can register, change or remove your preferences for commercial calls and messages by sending an SMS to the short code 1909, by calling 1909, through an IVR system, through a web portal that uses OTP verification, or through a mobile app approved by TRAI. It points you to your own operator's website for the details of each option.

Keep DND and fraud reporting separate: even with DND, report fraud calls and messages on Chakshu as well.

What to do next

  1. Turn on "Filter spam calls" and check Caller ID and spam.
  2. Block and report each spam call and text as it comes.
  3. Report fraud calls and messages on Chakshu within 30 days.
  4. If money has gone, report it on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in straight away.
